🍎Lifetime: $39.99 → Free 🍎

You know that feeling when you want a puzzle that actually makes you think...

But not one that's screaming for your attention with flashing rewards, countdown timers, and twelve different currencies?

Sometimes you just want a quiet challenge.

That’s exactly what Lexoku delivers.

Lexoku takes the satisfying logic of Sudoku and gives it a clever twist: instead of numbers, you're working with letters from a word.

Maybe it's a five-letter word like BRAIN. Maybe it's something longer like HARMONY.

Your goal is simple: place the letters into the grid so every row and column contains the exact letters of the word at the correct frequency.

Sounds easy.

Then suddenly you're twenty minutes deep, staring at one square and questioning everything.

A few reasons puzzle fans are loving it:
• Daily Challenge with a fresh puzzle every day
• Game Center leaderboards to compare solve times
• Weekly themed puzzle packs released every Monday
• Over 6,000 hand-curated puzzles
• Multiple difficulty levels whenever you want them
• No timers forcing you to rush
• No vocabulary tests or trivia knowledge required
• Relaxing, single-player experience built around pure logic

What makes Lexoku special is how calm it feels.

No pressure. No punishment. No losing streaks.

Just one more puzzle... and then somehow another one after that.

If you enjoy Sudoku, word games, logic puzzles, or simply having something thoughtful to unwind with, this one is dangerously easy to get hooked on.

Quietly addictive is probably the perfect description.

Just launched the MacOS version of my time-tracking desktop app, Duree! https://t.co/ivPGlMAcP3

I made Duree since I wanted a local-first app to help me track the time I spend on different activities (writing, working, reading). Most time tracking apps out there seem built more for tracking billable hours instead of personal activities, so I built the software I wanted. A few features I'm proud of:

- Local first. All data is stored on your machine in sqlite. No internet connection needed.
- Simple. Duree just tracks time for different activities, nothing else.
- Cross platform (Windows + MacOS, iOS + Android coming soon). I mainly work on my PC and Macbook, so it was important to me that I can track time on both devices.
- Sync (coming soon). I want to start a focus timer on my PC and then stop it on my phone. This will be a paid feature since it involves a server, but Duree will always be 100% free for local use.

Stay tuned for mobile releases + multi-device sync!

originalText:
A fatal crash and a federal probe hitting the tape, yet the stock doesn't even flinch—and honestly, the market is pricing this exactly right.

I see exactly why the desk is holding $TSLA completely flat today.

If you are trading the consensus bull case, this isn't an automotive manufacturer, it is a localized AI monopoly.

In that specific framework, a wrongful death lawsuit isn't a structural risk to the business model.

It is just an unfortunate R&D tax.

You price it like a pure software company, meaning you accept real-world beta-testing casualties because the terminal value of the code is supposedly infinite.

Makes total sense on paper.

But I am looking at the actual headline crossing the terminal right now, and the NTSB is leading the probe.

This is where the entire software-multiple thesis quietly falls apart.

The federal government does not regulate SaaS platforms.

If the NTSB decides your autonomous driving suite isn't a beta program but a lethal HARDWARE defect, you don't get to just push an over-the-air patch.

The entire valuation relies on the legal system treating a two-ton kinetic missile like a quirky iPhone app.

So if Washington suddenly forces them to absorb traditional automotive liability... what exactly is the bid when the tech premium goes to ZERO?
